reason: E1–E3 show that sliding in UHV on CoCrFeMnNi forms an ultra-nanocrystalline layer and gives low friction/wear via inverse Hall-Petch, but they explicitly exclude oxidation and do not address corrosion or passive film formation. E4 discusses passivation in a different HEA in acid, not under sliding, and does not link to nanocrystalline structure. Thus, the core premise that the refined layer promotes a protective passive film that synergistically reduces wear and corrosion is unsupported by the cited evidence.
premises: Sliding induces ultra-nanocrystalline/amorphous layer in HEAs
This refined layer promotes rapid, uniform passive oxide formation
The passive film reduces both wear and corrosion synergistically
Microalloyed variant outperforms CoCrFeMnNi in tribo-corrosion
Inverse Hall-Petch and dynamic amorphization occur in CoCrFeMnNi
